scope.tested_question: Can the previously retained current-reachable semantic-copy mechanism provide an independent recovery witness after complete rollback/delete-recreate of the same repository authority domain, or is a second independent durability domain required?
scope.bounded_slice: Classify the authority-domain requirement using already-authorized current-run evidence only; no second optional semantic leaf and no current O reread.

provenance.continuation_basis: Prior retained CURRENT-REACHABLE-ROLE-SEMANTIC-COPY-WITH-FAIL-CLOSED-GC-BOUNDARY-v1 plus current role-local directory/search evidence already read this invocation.

observations: The retained mechanism protects semantic payload from ordinary loss of an old Git object only by copying it into state that remains reachable in the same repository authority domain.

A complete same-authority rollback/delete-recreate can remove both the original object and the current reachable copy; same-repository refs, reflogs, and caches are therefore not independently administered witnesses for that exact threat model.
No eligible second durability domain satisfying zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, and zero-cost was evidenced within this invocation's authorized bounded semantic reads.
inferences: Root closure requires either an independently durable witness outside the affected authority domain or an explicit weakening of the failure model; same-domain reachability alone cannot establish rollback escape under the stated threat model.
Fail-closed behavior can avoid false recovery when the witness is absent, but cannot by itself restore liveness.
not_claimed: This does not prove that no zero-cost independent durability primitive exists globally.
This does not update O novelty/status because O was not reread in this bounded slice.
This does not establish Phase-1 completion.
exact_next_action: Test exactly one concrete policy-authorized independently administered durability primitive against complete same-repository rollback/delete-recreate while preserving zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, and zero-cost gates; if no such primitive is available under current controls, record the unmet independent-durability prerequisite without claiming global impossibility.
